allergy_answer: Penicillin: my throat swelled up and I collapsed in 2015.
reason_answer: To have my gallbladder taken out.

presentation.summary: Mrs Amna Hashmi, 45, is booked for keyhole gallbladder removal. She is well. In 2015 penicillin caused throat swelling and collapse.

history.answer: Three attacks of pain under my right ribs after oily meals; the scan showed gallstones.
No fever, no yellow eyes, no dark urine.
One caesarean section years ago, no problems with the anaesthetic.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.
Not pregnant; last period 10 days ago.

examination.finding: Red allergy band on the wrist: penicillin.
Soft, mildly tender under the right ribs, no guarding.

problems.label: Severe immediate penicillin allergy (throat swelling and collapse, 2015)
problems.why: A wrong antibiotic could cause anaphylaxis; the reaction must be recorded exactly and be visible to everyone.
expected_actions: Allergy band on and the record updated
Tell the anaesthetist and the pharmacist
If an antibiotic is needed, the prescriber chooses by the hospital allergy rule

problems.label: Low-risk planned operation: an antibiotic is probably not needed
problems.why: The allergy matters most if an antibiotic is prescribed; the simulator does not decide that.
expected_actions: Note the plan for the prescriber

decisions.prompt: She says penicillin once made her throat swell and she collapsed. What now?

options.text: Record the exact reaction, check the allergy band and tell the anaesthetist and pharmacist
options.consequence: Matches the book: severe immediate allergy, record the reaction.

options.text: Write 'allergy' in the notes and say nothing else
options.consequence: A vague entry hides how severe the reaction was.

decisions.prompt: The team asks which antibiotic she can have if one is needed.

options.text: The prescriber chooses according to the hospital penicillin-allergy rule; the trainee does not pick a drug
options.consequence: Matches the book; the choice is institutional and clinician-controlled.

options.text: Suggest a penicillin-family drug because it is the usual choice
options.consequence: Risk of anaphylaxis in a patient with a severe reaction.

correct: Ask the reaction and record it
Antibiotic choice left to the prescriber and the hospital rule

incorrect.shows: The nurse asks what the allergy was
incorrect.risk: Later staff cannot judge its severity

recovery: Ask again, record the reaction, update the band and the notes

debrief.priority: Severe immediate penicillin allergy (throat swelling and collapse, 2015)
debrief.why_priority: A wrong antibiotic could cause anaphylaxis; the reaction must be recorded exactly and be visible to everyone.
debrief.related: The findings in this case point to the same cause
debrief.trigger_escalation: Any value outside its safe band or any breach of a safety rule
debrief.if_ignored: Harm from the missed problem or an unsafe operation
debrief.remember: A severe allergy is recorded exactly and checked before every drug.
